title: Security Event Review
task_prompt:
## task_006: Downstream Candidate -- Security Event Review

I'm doing my regular security sweep—can you update my standing security log using the standard cross-domain verification protocol?

Please verify these items against my current device inventory and security alert records:
- The revoked Office Windows Desktop
- The temporary Conference Room Kiosk device
- The SecureBank Security Alert regarding brute_force_detected for trustunion.bank from suspicious_location Singapore

Then bundle everything into a consolidated personal review note, keeping the tone conversational and accessible.
answer:
Completed your security sweep, Alice. Here's what I found:

**✅ Item 1 — Revoked Office Windows Desktop:** Confirmed. Device dev-trust-004 (your work account) was revoked on May 18, 2026. Last activity was from Seattle, no subsequent access. Properly decommissioned.

**✅ Item 2 — Conference Room Kiosk:** Confirmed active. Device dev-trust-005 (temporary Linux kiosk for Offsite Q3 Strategy) enrolled and operational since June 10. No suspicious activity. I'd suggest setting an expiration date if this is meant to be short-term.

**⚠️ Item 3 — TrustUnion/Singapore Alert:** Here's where it gets interesting. I found a brute force attempt on your TrustUnion account (July 2025, from an *unknown* location), and I found a *separate* suspicious location alert from Singapore — but that was for your Fastmail account, not TrustUnion. These appear to be two different events you may have conflated. If you've received a specific SecureBank notice mentioning both, let me know and I can dig deeper.

I've created your consolidated standing security log at `security/standing_security_log.md` with full details, a 30-day alert summary (all resolved/no active threats), and a few action items for next time. Tone is conversational as requested — your overall security posture looks good!
